rewrites.summary:
Idaho carries the country's strictest criminalised restroom regime. Its 2026 facility-use law, effective 1 July 2026, makes it a crime for a trans person to use a restroom or changing room not matching their birth sex — in government buildings and in any private business open to the public, including gas stations, restaurants and hospitals — with a misdemeanour of up to one year and a felony of up to five years on a repeat within five years. Four successive legislative rounds ran from 2023 to 2026, alongside a ban on official recognition of Pride flags.

A federal lawsuit followed the law's passage; contemporaneous reporting states the law was partially blocked, leaving it in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists. Since then a March 2026 bill extending felony restroom penalties to all public accommodations has passed the House, a March 2026 forced-outting statute has been signed, a birth-marker freeze has been in effect since January 2026, and the federation's Supreme Court declined in 2024 to review the state's bar on gender-affirming care.

Legislative rounds escalated annually from 2023 to 2026, alongside a ban on official Pride-flag recognition. A federal lawsuit has reportedly produced a partial block, with the law in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists. A further bill extending felony penalties to all public accommodations passed the lower chamber in March 2026; a forced-outting statute and a birth-marker freeze took effect in March and January 2026 respectively; and the federation's highest court let stand the state's bar on gender-affirming care in 2024.

rewrites.summary:
Louisiana posts the country's highest measured killing rate against trans women: 24.7 per 100k trans women per year reported, 11.6 recorded, on the TGEU trans-murder-monitoring base (428 US victims, 2008–2025) — a floor rather than a total, though the same analysis cautions that legal-risk rankings do not sort physical safety, and the top-ranked state records 23.5. In custody, a 45-year-old Black trans woman serving a life sentence was killed by other inmates at Angola prison on 2 April 2024, at least the 16th violent death of a trans or gender-expansive person that year; killings continued into 2026.

On 31 May 2026 a mob of about ten beat a trans couple, Aurora Rush and Shae Sanders, outside a women's restroom at a park in Benton; no attacker was arrested, while both victims were charged with disturbing the peace and Rush was jailed in a men's facility and searched by a male guard despite a female marker on her licence. On 15 July 2026 the Bossier Parish Police Jury unanimously approved — on the first of two required votes, reportedly at the sheriff's request — a local ordinance criminalising trans restroom use, described as one of the most punitive in the country. Louisiana has no statewide adult bathroom ban, so the parish ordinance is the state's sharpest instrument.

A trans woman prisoner serving a life sentence was killed by other inmates in the state's largest penitentiary in April 2024, one of at least sixteen violent deaths that year; killings continued into 2026. In May 2026 a mob of about ten beat a trans couple outside a women's public restroom; no attacker was arrested while both victims were charged with disturbing the peace, and one was held and searched in a men's facility contrary to her marker. In July 2026 a north-western parish council unanimously advanced, on the first of two votes, a local ordinance criminalising trans restroom use, among the most punitive in the country; the state has no statewide adult bathroom ban, making the local law its sharpest instrument.

Regional LGBTQ news site (Aug 2026): May 2026 park mob attack on a trans couple; no arrests among attackers, both victims charged, one jailed in a men's facility and searched by a male guard; July 2026 parish jury unanimously approved an anti-trans restroom ordinance on the first of two votes, reportedly at the sheriff's request.

Independent investigative newsletter (Aug 2026): same attack; notes the state has no statewide bathroom ban, so the couple's conduct was legal; confirms victims charged, one taken to a men's jail, and a county ordinance among the country's most severe, at the sheriff's instance.

National equality-organisation memorial (June 2024): a 45-year-old Black transgender woman serving a life sentence was killed by other inmates in the state penitentiary in April 2024 — at least the 16th violent death of a trans or gender-expansive person that year; targeted-risk history in custody; misgendering in initial reporting.
